prompt: Create a cross-platform UI spec for a medication refill screen used by older adults. High trust, accessibility-sensitive, supports multiple medications and pharmacy pickup or delivery.
response_excerpt: Quality target: 5/5. The first glance is medication name, refill eligibility, and safety status; second glance is quantity, pharmacy, and pickup/delivery choice; final action is Request refill. Use 20-24sp/pt title, 17sp/pt body, 15-16sp/pt metadata, 24dp/pt section separation, 48dp/44pt minimum controls, semantic warning/error states with icon + text, and large-text layouts that keep dosage and contraindication warnings visible. Define default, too-early, requires doctor approval, interaction-warning, pharmacy-unavailable, offline, partial-success, submitted, and cancelled states. Include iOS and Android notes for back behavior, system date/time pickers, TalkBack/VoiceOver order, token names, analytics events, and QA across 200% text, dark mode, increased contrast, and localization.
expected_rationale: The response goes beyond shippable by anticipating high-trust healthcare edge cases, older-adult accessibility, platform behavior, localization, analytics, and design-system handoff.
improvement_suggestions: Validate clinical content and regulatory copy with the product/legal team.
Run task-based usability testing with older adults before release.
